clues.name: American Robin
clues.fact: With an estimated 370 million birds, it's the most abundant landbird in North America, ahead of red-winged blackbirds and starlings.

clues.name: Mule Deer
clues.fact: Named for its big, mule-like ears, it's often seen stotting, with all four feet coming down together.

clues.name: Ochre Sea Star
clues.fact: Remove it from a stretch of shore and California mussels take over almost completely, which is why it's called a keystone species.

clues.name: Aggregating Anemone
clues.fact: Rival clone colonies fight with special stinging tentacles, and a scout polyp that comes home badly stung may be attacked by its own clonemates.

clues.name: Pacific Banana Slug
clues.fact: Though it tends to avoid slime trails, even its own, it can find its way back to the same spot after long periods away.

clues.name: Olympic Marmot
clues.fact: Found only on Washington's Olympic Peninsula, this cat-sized marmot became the state's official endemic mammal in 2009.

rounds.name: Mount Rainier National Park
rounds.official: Mount Rainier National Park, US, WA

clues.name: Red-tailed Hawk
clues.fact: TV shows often use its rasping scream as a generic raptor sound, even when the bird on screen isn't a red-tailed hawk.

clues.name: Steller's Jay
clues.fact: A noted mimic, it often imitates the calls of red-tailed hawks and ospreys, sending other birds fleeing for cover.

clues.name: Black-tailed Bumble Bee
clues.fact: Northern bees wear a red band on the abdomen that's earned them the nickname 'red butts', while southern bees are black there instead.

clues.name: Douglas's Squirrel
clues.fact: Native Americans of the Kings River called it the 'Pillillooeet', copying the sound of its alarm call.

clues.name: Northwestern Salamander
clues.fact: Gilled adults get more common with altitude, so lowland adults almost all live on land while most at very high elevations keep their gills.

clues.name: Cascade Golden-mantled Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: The Columbia River walls it off from its closest relative, and that isolation likely explains how the two became separate species.

clues.name: House Finch
clues.fact: Sold illegally in New York City as 'Hollywood finches,' birds released in the 1940s went on to settle across the eastern United States.

clues.name: White-winged Dove
clues.fact: North America's only game bird that's also a migratory pollinator, it leans heavily on saguaro nectar and fruit where the cactus grows.

clues.name: Common Side-blotched Lizard
clues.fact: In its rock-paper-scissors mating game, yellow-throated males mimic females to sneak matings from the harems of big orange-throated males.

clues.name: Desert Spiny Lizard
clues.fact: A frequent tree climber, it favors cottonwoods, yuccas, Joshua trees and ironwood, and is often seen doing territorial push-ups.

clues.name: Gambel's Quail
clues.fact: Often confused with the California quail, the male gives itself away with a black patch on the lower breast that California quail lack.

clues.name: Stripe-tailed Scorpion
clues.fact: Brownish-tan stripes along its tail set it apart from the Arizona bark scorpion, and its venom isn't considered dangerous to people.

clues.name: Great Blue Heron
clues.fact: In South Florida, the Florida Keys and the Caribbean, some are all white, a population known as the great white heron.

clues.name: Green Anole
clues.fact: Its ancestors crossed the sea from Cuba to the southern United States, a rare case of an island lizard colonizing a mainland.

clues.name: American Alligator
clues.fact: When water starts to freeze, it pokes its snout through the surface to breathe above the ice and can stay that way for days.

clues.name: Brown Anole
clues.fact: In the US it has pushed the native green anole up into the treetops, and it sometimes eats green anole hatchlings too.

clues.name: Florida Red-bellied Cooter
clues.fact: Known for sometimes laying its eggs in alligator nest mounds, it has a red-tinged belly and two toothlike cusps on its upper beak.

clues.name: Peters's Rock Agama
clues.fact: By eating Florida's invasive brown anoles, it may leave mosquitoes fewer to feed on and send them after people, a 2024 study suggests.

clues.name: Canada Goose
clues.fact: A common park bird, it's often called a pest for its droppings, noise, aggression and habit of stalking and begging for food.

clues.name: Coyote
clues.fact: Coyotes sometimes team up with American badgers to dig out rodents, and some have been seen resting their heads on their badger partners.

clues.name: Black-billed Magpie
clues.fact: Once tied to bison herds, it now lands on the backs of cattle to pick off ticks and insects.

clues.name: American Bison
clues.fact: From 1980 to 1999, bison injured 79 people in Yellowstone, more than three times the 24 hurt by bears.

clues.name: Uinta Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: Only active for a few months each year, adults head back underground to hibernate between late July and mid-August.

rounds.name: Joshua Tree National Park
rounds.official: Joshua Tree National Park, US, CA

clues.name: Turkey Vulture
clues.fact: Flying low, it can sniff out the gases that dead animals give off in the early stages of decay.

clues.name: White-lined Sphinx
clues.fact: Some Native Americans skewered and roasted its caterpillars, which have almost as much fat as hamburger meat but nearly a third less saturated fat.

clues.name: White-crowned Sparrow
clues.fact: During migration it can stay half-awake for up to two weeks, a trick studied for keeping shift workers and truck drivers alert.

clues.name: Western Fence Lizard
clues.fact: Ticks carrying Lyme disease that feed on it come away clean, because a protein in its blood kills the bacterium in their gut.

clues.name: Costa's Hummingbird
clues.fact: The male's purple throat feathers flare back behind his head, and he angles his courtship dives to the sun to show them off.

clues.name: Inflated Beetle
clues.fact: Its inflated wing covers, black with dense white spots, are fused down the middle, so this beetle can't fly.

clues.name: Canada Jay
clues.fact: Each summer it glues thousands of bits of food into bark and lichen with sticky saliva, then finds them by memory, sometimes months later.

clues.name: Alaskan Fritillary
clues.fact: Also called the mountain fritillary, it's found in North America and northern European Russia, and its caterpillars eat false bistort and alpine smartweed.

clues.name: Arctic White
clues.fact: Males look mostly white from above but can be pale yellow underneath with dark green veins, while females can be white or yellow.

clues.name: Arctic Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: In hibernation its core body temperature drops below freezing, colder than any other hibernating mammal, and its heart beats about once a minute.

clues.name: Collared Pika
clues.fact: It spends much of the summer stacking plants into haypiles for winter, but some have been seen eating dead birds for fat and protein.

clues.name: Thinhorn Sheep
clues.fact: Denali National Park and Preserve was created in 1917 to protect these sheep from overhunting, and they're still often seen there.

rounds.name: Great Smoky Mountains
rounds.official: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, NC, US

clues.name: Dark-eyed Junco
clues.fact: A flock of these juncos is sometimes called a blizzard, which suits a bird whose scientific name means 'winter junco'.

clues.name: White-tailed Deer
clues.fact: Bambi is a roe deer in the original novel, but Disney's 1942 film made him a white-tailed deer.

clues.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
clues.fact: John White drew one on Sir Walter Raleigh's 1587 expedition to Virginia, the first known drawing of a North American butterfly.

clues.name: Eastern Fence Lizard
clues.fact: It twitches to throw off attacking fire ants before fleeing, and in some regions it has evolved longer legs to escape them.

clues.name: Seal Salamander
clues.fact: The monticola in its scientific name is Latin for 'mountaineer' or 'highlander', after the high elevations where it's commonly found.

clues.name: Blue Ridge Two-lined Salamander
clues.fact: Bright yellow to orange, it has two black lines along its back that usually break into dots around the middle of its long tail.

rounds.name: Big Bend National Park
rounds.official: Big Bend National Park, US, TX

clues.name: Northern Cardinal
clues.fact: Defending his territory, a male may mistake his reflection in a shiny surface for an invading rival and fight it relentlessly.

clues.name: Vermilion Flycatcher
clues.fact: A favorite with birders, it's rarely kept in aviaries because captive males tend to lose their vermilion red, likely a matter of diet.

clues.name: Greater Roadrunner
clues.fact: Early in the morning it sunbathes, back to the sun and feathers ruffled to bare its black skin, sometimes for two or three hours.

clues.name: Black-crested Titmouse
clues.fact: It nests mostly in old woodpecker holes, whether in living or dead trees, fence posts or utility poles.

clues.name: Eastern Black-tailed Rattlesnake
clues.fact: True to its name, its tail scales are entirely black, no matter what color the rest of the snake is.

clues.name: Canyon Lizard
clues.fact: It lives on the rock faces of canyon walls, sheltering in crevices, and its gray, tan or reddish-brown back matches the rock.

rounds.name: Point Reyes
rounds.official: Point Reyes National Seashore, US, CA

clues.name: Song Sparrow
clues.fact: Its fear of hawks and owls seems to be instinctive, but a song sparrow has to learn to be afraid of cats.

clues.name: Great Horned Owl
clues.fact: A poor sense of smell lets it routinely attack skunks with impunity, and its nests often reek of skunk.

clues.name: Black Phoebe
clues.fact: Always near water, it cements its open cup nest in place with mud under a cliff or a bridge.

clues.name: California Scrub-Jay
clues.fact: It summons other jays to screech over a dead jay, and these noisy 'funerals' can last up to half an hour.

clues.name: Gray Buckeye
clues.fact: Its wing eyespots distract predators just like the common buckeye's, and until 2018 it was counted as part of that species.

clues.name: Button's Banana Slug
clues.fact: With no shell and a bright, banana-like color, it's protected by toxic slime that numbs the mouth of anything that eats it.

clues.name: Convergent Lady Beetle
clues.fact: In the western United States, it may spend up to nine months dormant in large groups in mountain valleys.

clues.name: Phimenes curvatus
clues.fact: A potter wasp, it belongs to a group found across the Indomalayan and Australasian regions.

clues.name: Hawaiian Goose
clues.fact: Its toes are less webbed than a typical goose's, an adaptation for walking on the cooled lava of its volcanic home.

clues.name: Amarygmus morio
clues.fact: Its wireworm-shaped larvae are shiny and mostly yellow-brown, and some have been collected from the trunk of a rotting mango tree.

clues.name: ʻIʻiwi
clues.fact: Its song has been likened to whistles, balls dropping into water, balloons rubbing together and the squeak of a rusty hinge.

clues.name: Eupithecia monticolens
clues.fact: This Hawaiian moth lives on six of the islands and nowhere else, and its caterpillars feed on plants such as Metrosideros and Pipturus.

clues.name: American Black Bear
clues.fact: In experiments, black bears learned to tell colors apart faster than chimpanzees and just as fast as domestic dogs.

clues.name: Monarch
clues.fact: Eastern monarchs fly thousands of miles south to Florida and Mexico each fall, and it takes several generations to return north in spring.

clues.name: American Toad
clues.fact: Fish have reportedly died after eating just one of its toxic tadpoles, but most fish quickly learn to leave them alone.

clues.name: Northern Azure
clues.fact: On the wing from April to July, it ranges from the Maritimes south along the Appalachians to West Virginia.

clues.name: Mink Frog
clues.fact: Named for its scent, said to resemble a mink's, it smells more like rotting onions to anyone who's never sniffed a mink.

clues.name: Frosted Whiteface
clues.fact: Like every whiteface, it gets the 'whiteface' in its name from the distinctive pale frons at the front of its head.

clues.name: Red-winged Blackbird
clues.fact: When researchers dyed males' red shoulder patches black, 64% lost their territories, compared with just 8% of the control birds.

clues.name: Wapiti
clues.fact: The name wapiti comes from a Shawnee and Cree word for 'white rump', the pale patch it fluffs up to signal alarm.

clues.name: Hoary Marmot
clues.fact: Whistler, British Columbia, once called London Mountain, was renamed after this marmot, nicknamed 'the whistler' for its high-pitched alarm call.

clues.name: Anicia Checkerspot
clues.fact: Plant chemicals eaten as a caterpillar stay in its body, and its red, yellow and black bands warn predators that it tastes bad.

clues.name: Columbian Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: Nicknamed 'seven sleepers' for their long hibernation, they greet each other by touching mouths and noses, which looks a lot like kissing.

clues.name: Banff Springs Snail
clues.fact: Found in a few Banff hot springs and nowhere else, it can dwindle until the entire population fits in an ice cream cone.

clues.name: Great-tailed Grackle
clues.fact: The Aztecs brought it to Tenochtitlan around 1500, probably for its iridescent feathers, and that's the earliest documented bird introduction in the Americas.

clues.name: Brown Basilisk
clues.fact: Smaller ones can sprint about 10 to 20 meters across water without sinking, opening flaps on their hind feet for extra surface area.

clues.name: Central American Agouti
clues.fact: Agoutis placed fourth for sense of smell in an analysis of 240 species, beating dogs, which came out only average.

clues.name: Bare-throated Tiger-Heron
clues.fact: Its bare throat is greenish-yellow to orange at every age, and males give a booming call, especially at sunset.

clues.name: Mantled Howler Monkey
clues.fact: Disturb one and it'll often show its irritation by urinating or defecating on you, with good aim from high in the trees.

clues.name: Strawberry Poison Dart Frog
clues.fact: Mothers carry each tadpole to its own pool of water, often in a bromeliad, then feed it unfertilized eggs that pass on their toxins.

clues.name: Tropical Kingbird
clues.fact: The melancholicus in its name means melancholic, or bad-tempered, and it aggressively defends its territory even against frigatebirds, toucans and hawks.

clues.name: Hoatzin
clues.fact: Chicks escape predators by dropping into the water and swimming away, then climb back to the nest with the two claws on each wing.

clues.name: Yellow-banded Pinktoe Tarantula
clues.fact: Often mistaken for Avicularia juruensis, it has brighter yellow leg rings, and an antifungal peptide in its venom was named juruin after the mix-up.

clues.name: Black-capped Squirrel Monkey
clues.fact: Females run its big troops and push the males out to the edges, unlike the common squirrel monkey, whose troops are male-dominated.

clues.name: Black-faced Spider Monkey
clues.fact: Almost thumbless, with a gripping tail up to a meter long, it moves through the trees with an agility only Asia's gibbons can match.

clues.name: Puna Thistletail
clues.fact: Males and females both sing a quick run of spluttering high notes that speeds up and grows louder, then fades at the end.
clues.by: Christoph Moning, bazı hakları saklıdır (CC BY), yükleyen: Christoph Moning

rounds.name: Torres del Paine
rounds.official: Parque Nacional Torres del Paine, MA, CL

clues.name: Chimango Caracara
clues.fact: The commonest raptor through much of Chile and Argentina, it often follows farmers as they plow, sometimes more than 100 birds at once.

clues.name: Austral Thrush
clues.fact: An accomplished mimic, it's known to imitate the songs of at least 12 other species, including songbirds and raptors.

clues.name: Crested Duck
clues.fact: Along the coast it forages for clams among rocks and kelp, while on the Altiplano it gathers on alkaline lakes thick with zooplankton.

clues.name: Upland Goose
clues.fact: Darwin noted in On the Origin of Species that the webbing between its toes seemed 'rudimentary in function, though not in structure'.

clues.name: Austral Smooth-throated lizard
clues.fact: One of the world's southernmost lizards, it lives on Patagonia's windswept steppe and gives birth to live young, usually three to five.

clues.name: Yellow-crowned Night Heron
clues.fact: Hunting crayfish, it stands at the burrow facing the sun, so its shadow doesn't fall across the entrance and warn its prey.

clues.name: Ecuadorian Hermit Crab
clues.fact: After nine hours with one food, it prefers foods that smell different for the next six, like a person bored with the same meal.

clues.name: Mexican Hogfish
clues.fact: Starting life as a female, it later becomes a male, and large males sport a pronounced hump between the eyes.

clues.name: Pacific Creolefish
clues.fact: Unlike most groupers, it schools in the water column and picks plankton one at a time, but it still hides in crevices from danger.

clues.name: Blue-footed Booby
clues.fact: When researchers dulled a male's blue feet with makeup after the first egg, his mate laid a smaller second one.

clues.name: Marine Iguana
clues.fact: During El Niño food shortages, it can shrink by up to a fifth of its length, then grow back when the algae return.

clues.name: Yellow-billed Teal
clues.fact: Drakes stretch up high after mating and swim around and alongside the female, a routine unique among its relatives.

clues.name: Guanaco
clues.fact: A teaspoon of guanaco blood holds about 68 million red blood cells, four times a human's, which helps the animal survive at high altitude.

clues.name: Imperial Shag
clues.fact: It nests in colonies often shared with rockhopper penguins and black-browed albatrosses, cementing seaweed and grass together with mud and droppings.

clues.name: Magellanic Oystercatcher
clues.fact: Disturbed near its nest, it may move off and sit on an imaginary one, false-brooding to draw attention away from its eggs and chicks.

clues.name: Magellanic Cormorant
clues.fact: Feeding close to shore along kelp beds, it typically dives only about 5 meters, leaving deeper water further out to the imperial shag.

clues.name: Dolphin Gull
clues.fact: It raids seabird nests left empty when people scare the parents off, and keeping humans away has been found to help nesting cormorants.

clues.name: African Savanna Elephant
clues.fact: A lower-ranking elephant greets its superior by putting the tip of its trunk into the other's mouth.

clues.name: Black-bellied Bustard
clues.fact: A courting male pulls his head onto his back with a wheezy whistle, then slowly raises it with a popping 'quock' and soft gurgling.

clues.name: Marabou Stork
clues.fact: Marabous living off garbage dumps will swallow virtually anything, and they've been seen eating shoes and pieces of metal.

clues.name: Olive Baboon
clues.fact: In Eritrea, olive baboons use water holes dug by elephants, while the elephants use baboons in the treetops as an early warning system.

clues.name: Maasai Giraffe
clues.fact: Tanzania's national animal, it has jagged, leaf-like blotches that run all the way from its hooves to its head.

clues.name: Mwanza Flat-headed Rock Agama
clues.fact: Males wear Spider-Man colors, a red or violet head and shoulders on a dark blue body, which has made the lizard a fashionable pet.

clues.name: Plains Zebra
clues.fact: The largest wild zebra herd outside Africa roams San Simeon, California, descended from animals left behind when Hearst Castle's private zoo closed.

clues.name: White-browed Robin-Chat
clues.fact: Usually sung at dawn and dusk, its song starts quietly and grows louder, with phrases like 'don't-you-do-it' sometimes repeated over ten times.

clues.name: Cheetah
clues.fact: Cheetahs vary so little genetically that skin grafts swapped between unrelated animals are accepted and heal, as if they shared the same genes.

clues.name: Gray Crowned-Crane
clues.fact: Along with the black crowned crane, it's the only crane that can roost in trees, thanks to a long hind toe that grips branches.

clues.name: Superb Starling
clues.fact: Check the eyes: pale creamy white on this one, red on the look-alike Hildebrandt's starling, which also lacks the white breast band.

clues.name: Rufous-tailed Weaver
clues.fact: Tanzania is the only country where it breeds, though wandering birds sometimes turn up in Kenya.

clues.name: Lion
clues.fact: In Ngorongoro Crater, lions live largely on kills stolen from hyenas, but in Botswana's Chobe National Park the hyenas do the stealing.

clues.name: Common Hippopotamus
clues.fact: For an animal that spends most of the day in water, it may not swim at all, walking or bouncing along the bottom instead.

clues.name: Impala
clues.fact: Seemingly the only hoofed mammal that grooms itself and others, it combs ticks from a partner's head and neck with its lower front teeth.

clues.name: Southern Giraffe
clues.fact: Also called the two-horned giraffe, it has rounded or blotched spots, some with star-like points, running all the way down to its hooves.

clues.name: Rainbow Skink
clues.fact: Three yellow-orange stripes run from its head to an electric blue tail, though in adults they can fade until they're hard to see.

clues.name: Brown-headed Parrot
clues.fact: The cryptoxanthus in its scientific name comes from Greek words for 'hidden yellow', after the bright yellow feathers under its wings.

rounds.name: Table Mountain
rounds.official: Table Mountain National Park, WC, ZA

clues.name: Common Ostrich
clues.fact: Its eyes are the largest of any land vertebrate, 50 millimetres across, which helps it spot predators at a great distance.

clues.name: Hadada Ibis
clues.fact: Named for its extremely loud haa-haa-haa-de-dah call, often given in flight as birds leave and return to roost trees.

clues.name: Rock Hyrax
clues.fact: Perfumers steep its hyraceum, a sticky mass of dung and urine used in South African folk medicine, in alcohol to make a natural musk.

clues.name: Cape Robin-Chat
clues.fact: Its harsh, three-syllable alarm call is behind local names like 'Jan frederik', which fits the rhythm if you run the last syllables together.

clues.name: Southern Rock Agama
clues.fact: Approached by a predator, a breeding male presses flat against the rock and swaps his bright blue head for duller camouflage colors.

clues.name: Southern Double-collared Sunbird
clues.fact: The male looks a lot like the greater double-collared sunbird but is smaller, with a narrower red chest band and a shorter bill.

clues.name: Common Warthog
clues.fact: It kneels on calloused pads on its wrists to graze, and those pads start forming before it's even born.

clues.name: Springbok
clues.fact: During droughts, millions of migrating springbok once formed herds hundreds of kilometers long that could take several days to pass a town.

clues.name: Gemsbok
clues.fact: New Mexico released 93 gemsbok between 1969 and 1977, and about 3,000 now live in the desert around the White Sands Missile Range.

clues.name: Namib Rock Agama
clues.fact: Orange-and-blue males court the dappled, checkered females by running in circles around them while bobbing their heads.

clues.name: Damara Dik-dik
clues.fact: Dik-diks are named for their call, a trumpet-like 'zik-zik' they give while zigzagging away from danger to a nearby thicket.

clues.name: Bare-cheeked Babbler
clues.fact: Especially common in Etosha, it lives in noisy family groups of 6 to 12 birds that mob predators together.

rounds.name: The Okavango Delta
rounds.official: Okavango Delta World Heritage Site, BW

clues.name: African Buffalo
clues.fact: Herds decide where to eat or drink by 'voting', with females standing up before dusk to point in a particular direction.

clues.name: Vervet Monkey
clues.fact: Leopards, martial eagles, rock pythons and baboons each get their own alarm call, which infants learn by observation alone.

clues.name: Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill
clues.fact: Walled into her nest with her own droppings, the female sheds every flight feather at once while the male feeds her through a slit.

clues.name: Wahlberg’s Striped Skink
clues.fact: The Wahlberg in its name was Johan August Wahlberg, a Swedish naturalist, and this skink gives birth to live young.

clues.name: Lechwe
clues.fact: Coated in a water-repellent substance, its legs let it run fast through the knee-deep water it uses for protection from predators.

clues.name: Angolan Reed Frog
clues.fact: Extremely abundant, it readily colonizes newly created water bodies and even turns up in towns and gardens.

clues.name: Pied Crow
clues.fact: The Maasai name for it, ol-korrok, comes from the sound of its harsh karh-karh-karh call.

clues.name: Redleg Orbweaver
clues.fact: Strong enough to snag the occasional bird or bat, its web is spun from yellow silk that shines like gold in sunlight.

clues.name: Panther Chameleon
clues.fact: Its color depends on where it lives, with panther chameleons from Nosy Be typically blue and those from Maroantsetra mostly red.

clues.name: Ring-tailed Lemur
clues.fact: Rival males hold stink fights, soaking their tails in scent from glands on their arms and waving them at each other.

clues.name: Striped Day Gecko
clues.fact: More colorful than the females, males are green with red splotches on the head and lower back and a dark band down each side.

clues.name: Carpet Chameleon
clues.fact: Fast-maturing and short-lived, it can breed about three months after hatching but rarely if ever lives past three years.

clues.name: Black-headed Gull
clues.fact: Mostly a bird of Europe and Asia, it also breeds in small numbers on the coast of eastern Canada.

clues.name: Arctic Fox
clues.fact: A yearling female tagged on Svalbard crossed the polar ice to Greenland and on to Canada, covering 3,506 km in 76 days.

clues.name: Icelandic Scallop
clues.fact: Subfossil shells of this North Atlantic scallop turn up south of its present range, including in the British Isles.

clues.name: Bearded Seal
clues.fact: In the breeding season males sing a long, warbling trill that ends in a moan and can be heard over 30 km away underwater.

clues.name: Walrus
clues.fact: An air sac under its throat works like a flotation bubble, letting it bob upright in the water and sleep.

clues.name: Eurasian Blackbird
clues.fact: Its name dates from when 'bird' meant a small bird and crows were 'fowl,' making it the only common black 'bird' in the British Isles.

clues.name: Common Whelk
clues.fact: Look on the beach for its washed-up egg cases, which people call sea wash balls.

clues.name: Atlantic Puffin
clues.fact: Colonies in Iceland hold 60% of the world's Atlantic puffins, and in their burrows they growl a bit like a chainsaw being revved up.

clues.name: Pink-footed Goose
clues.fact: Its most important breeding site, Þjórsárver in Iceland, wasn't found until 1951, when Peter Scott and his team went looking.

clues.name: Great Skua
clues.fact: It often robs gulls, terns and even northern gannets of their fish, and it'll fly at the head of anyone approaching its nest.
clues.by: Janne Asp, זכויות יוצרים חלקיות (CC BY-NC-ND), הועלה על ידי Janne Asp

clues.name: White-beaked Dolphin
clues.fact: With up to 92 vertebrae, it has more than any other oceanic dolphin, and it often rides the bow waves of fast boats.

rounds.name: Donana
rounds.official: RB ESP 04. Reserva de la Biosfera Doñana. Andalucia. España. , AN, ES

clues.name: Great Tit
clues.fact: Great tits are the first songbirds recorded preying on bats, killing hibernating pipistrelles in winter when other food is scarce and eating their brains.

clues.name: Yellow-legged Gull
clues.fact: When Italy's 2020 lockdown cut off their food scraps, Rome's yellow-legged gulls turned to hunting prey as large as rats and rock doves.

clues.name: European Serin
clues.fact: Serinus, its Latin name, comes from serin, the French word for a canary, which may be a corruption of citrinus, Latin for lemon-colored.

clues.name: Iberian Green Frog
clues.fact: The Sahara frog of North Africa is its closest living relative, and the two may have split when the Mediterranean dried up.

clues.name: Andalusian wall lizard
clues.fact: Swiss botanist Henri Vaucher is honored in its scientific name, and it lives from sea level up to 3,100 meters.

clues.name: Scarabaeus cicatricosus
clues.fact: Like its relative the sacred scarab, it feeds only on dung, rolling a piece away from the pile and burying it to eat underground.

rounds.name: The Camargue
rounds.official: Réserve Naturelle de Camargue, PACA, FR

clues.name: Great Crested Grebe
clues.fact: Pairs court each other with elaborate, synchronized dances, showing off striking black, orange-brown and white plumage.

clues.name: Speckled Wood
clues.fact: Northern speckled woods are bigger and darker than southern ones, with longer forewings that help them handle cooler temperatures.

clues.name: Egyptian Bird Grasshopper
clues.fact: One of Europe's largest grasshoppers, it's easy to identify by its eyes, which have vertical black and white stripes.

clues.name: Pimelia muricata
clues.fact: Fused body plates help it hold on to water, but they also leave it unable to fly.

clues.name: White Wagtail
clues.fact: The national bird of Latvia, it's adapted to towns by foraging for insects on paved areas like car parks.

clues.name: Red-backed Shrike
clues.fact: Frogs, lizards, small birds and large insects end up impaled on thorns or barbed wire in its larder, hence the nickname butcher bird.

clues.name: Dalmatian Pelican
clues.fact: The 'crispus' in its name is Latin for curly, after the shaggy crest that sets it apart from the smooth-headed great white pelican.

clues.name: Northern White-breasted Hedgehog
clues.fact: Size follows climate in this hedgehog: it grows larger in southern Europe than in the north, and smaller where summers are wetter.

clues.name: Vineyard Snail
clues.fact: Its scientific name comes from Vindobona, the Celtic settlement now known as Vienna, the capital of Austria.

clues.name: Eastern Tree Frog
clues.fact: Inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone, these tree frogs are much darker on the back, perhaps because the disaster's radiation favored dark skin.

clues.name: Red Deer
clues.fact: A rutting stag may guard as many as 20 hinds and rarely eats while he does, losing up to a fifth of his weight.

clues.name: European Toad
clues.fact: Normally solitary, toads gather in large numbers at certain breeding ponds, and some are killed on roads during these annual migrations.

clues.name: Roman Snail
clues.fact: Eaten by the ancient Romans and prized in French cooking as escargot, it's hard to farm and rarely raised commercially.

clues.name: grass snake
clues.fact: It can rear up and flatten its head and neck like a cobra, a trick that may date from when cobras lived in Europe.

clues.name: small balsam
clues.fact: Ripe seed pods explode when touched and fling the seeds widely, which is why it's also called small-flowered touch-me-not.

clues.name: Wisent
clues.fact: When poachers killed the last free-living wisent in 1927, Europe's heaviest wild land animal was down to 48, all in zoos.

clues.name: Western Marsh Harrier
clues.fact: Males often pair with two females and occasionally three, and most pair bonds last just a single breeding season.

clues.name: Common Buzzard
clues.fact: Described as 'sluggish and not very bold', a resident buzzard can spend more than half its day just sitting on a perch.

clues.name: Common Wood-Pigeon
clues.fact: In the UK and Ireland its cooing is remembered as 'take two cows, Teddy', though the call starts and ends partway through the phrase.

clues.name: Banded Wedge Shell
clues.fact: Underwater video shows it's most active around low tide, when it 'leaps' and gets dragged around by the waves before burying itself again.

clues.name: Brown Shrimp
clues.fact: Its numbers at Lytham in Lancashire tracked the yearly sunspot count so closely from 1965 to 1975 that sunspots can help predict the catch.

clues.name: Flying Crab
clues.fact: It feeds on crustaceans, especially young Crangon shrimp, as well as molluscs and fish, and can host the parasitic barnacle Sacculina.

clues.name: Common Chaffinch
clues.fact: After farmers thresh their crops, it sometimes spends weeks picking grain out of the discarded chaff, which likely gave it its name.

clues.name: European Robin
clues.fact: Territorial fights cause up to 10% of adult robin deaths in some areas, and robins have even been recorded attacking their own reflection.

clues.name: Tapered Drone Fly
clues.fact: Check the feet: on the front and middle legs they're entirely yellow, and males have a triangular abdomen, females a squarish one.

clues.name: Smoky Wainscot
clues.fact: Hard to tell for certain from similar wainscots, it has buff forewings with a dark streak near the base and gray hindwings edged white.

clues.name: Magpie Moth
clues.fact: Research on this moth, which comes in many different forms, is what first revealed sex-linked traits.

clues.name: Mountain Bumble Bee
clues.fact: It nests underground in abandoned small-mammal burrows, and its colonies are small, often with fewer than 50 workers.

clues.name: Oriental Turtle-Dove
clues.fact: The Ainu traditionally hear its call as a saying: 'turtle dove ploughs, grandmother draws water, wife cooks, little master eats'.

clues.name: Eastern Spot-billed Duck
clues.fact: Since the early 1900s its range in Japan and the Russian Far East has spread over 500 kilometers north, possibly because of global warming.

clues.name: Red-crowned Crane
clues.fact: China shortlisted it for national animal, but the decision was put off over its scientific name, Grus japonensis, which means Japanese crane.

clues.name: Carabus gehinii
clues.fact: Hunting snails at night, Carabus beetles like this one either crush the shell or push their heads inside to eat.

clues.name: Common Mapwing
clues.fact: Its domed eggs have a toothed lid like a cogwheel, which the caterpillar lifts to climb out, leaving the shell uneaten.
clues.by: Alan Kwok (King Lun), Ada Tai (Ah Heung) / 阿達蘭 AdAlan

clues.name: Pale Grass Blue
clues.fact: After the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, Japanese studies found more abnormalities in pale grass blues exposed to the radiation.

clues.name: Brown-eared Bulbul
clues.fact: One author described its song as 'one of the most unattractive noises made by any bird'.

clues.name: Brown Amur Goby
clues.fact: Guarding eggs under a rock for up to two weeks without feeding, a worn-out male may end up eating them.

clues.name: Camponotus hemichlaena
clues.fact: Carpenter ants like this one don't eat wood, and despite the name, only a few kinds even nest in it.

clues.name: Blueberry Hermit Crab
clues.fact: Blue to purple with pale eyestalks, it chirps at a high pitch by rapidly beating the tip of its body inside its shell.

clues.name: Japanese Angelfish
clues.fact: Females turn into males when they reach 12.7 cm long, and the switch takes 20 to 39 days to finish.

clues.name: Wrought Iron Butterflyfish
clues.fact: Unusually black for a butterflyfish, it sometimes gathers in huge numbers to graze in a tight, rippling 'wrought-iron ball'.

clues.name: Bonin White-eye
clues.fact: Offered tinned peaches, it wouldn't touch them until it saw introduced warbling white-eyes eating them.
clues.by: shoko noiman, bazı hakları saklıdır (CC BY-NC), yükleyen: shoko noiman

clues.name: Bonin Flying-fox
clues.fact: One of the northernmost flying foxes, it spends winter days in colonies of up to 100, packed into a ball to keep warm.

rounds.name: Kakadu National Park
rounds.official: Kakadu National Park World Heritage Site, NT, AU

clues.name: Little Pied Cormorant
clues.fact: In New Zealand the mostly black, white-throated form wins out, and even in Northland only about one in four birds is pied.

clues.name: Saltwater Crocodile
clues.fact: Its broad body had early observers taking it for an alligator, which is why northern Australia's Alligator Rivers carry the wrong reptile's name.

clues.name: Freshwater Crocodile
clues.fact: A slender snout sets it apart from the saltwater crocodile, and it can live where its bigger relative can't, like above Kakadu's escarpment.

clues.name: Northern Fantail
clues.fact: French ornithologist Louis Vieillot named it rufiventris, Modern Latin for 'red-bellied', from a specimen he wrongly believed came from Australia.

clues.name: Pied Heron
clues.fact: Without the adult's crest and dark head, young birds can pass for small white-necked herons and were once classified as a separate species.

clues.name: Eastern Short-eared Rock Wallaby
clues.fact: Once lumped in with the Kimberley's short-eared rock-wallaby, it's smaller and darker, with brighter limbs and bolder stripes on its head and flanks.

clues.name: Climbing Galaxias
clues.fact: Broad, downward-facing fins let it climb waterfalls and dam sluices, and young fish netted as whitebait can scramble up and out of buckets.

clues.name: Laughing Kookaburra
clues.fact: Its laughing territorial call, often given by several birds at once, is widely used as a stock jungle sound effect.

clues.name: Superb Fairywren
clues.fact: Males pluck yellow petals and show them to females, sometimes in other territories and even outside the breeding season.

clues.name: Bare-nosed Wombat
clues.fact: Besides leaving cube-shaped dung, it digs burrows up to 20 meters long that echidnas, wallabies, birds and even koalas also use.

clues.name: Rufous-bellied Pademelon
clues.fact: It's been reported standing upright to yank up clumps of grass and throw them against its chest, possibly as a signal.

clues.name: Tasmanian Devil
clues.fact: Tasmania's early explorers heard its far-carrying screeches at night before they ever saw one, and nicknamed it 'Beelzebub's pup'.

rounds.name: The Great Otway
rounds.official: Great Otway National Park, VIC AU

clues.name: Koala
clues.fact: Its eucalyptus diet is low in nutrition and toxic enough to deter most other mammals, and it sleeps up to twenty hours a day.

clues.name: Crimson Rosella
clues.fact: In the breeding season, females often raid other rosellas' nests and destroy the eggs, the most common reason an egg fails to hatch.

clues.name: Common Brown
clues.fact: Climate change has it emerging ten days earlier in the year than it did 65 years ago.

clues.name: Common Halfband
clues.fact: Often confused with Simosyrphus grandicornis, Australia's other most common hoverfly, it's told apart by its all-black thorax.

clues.name: Otway Black Snail
clues.fact: A carnivore, it grips other snails, slugs and earthworms with rows of sharp, backward-pointing teeth, but it won't eat its own kind.
